title: Agent-driven recursive patch subdivision
description:
Allow the voyage agent (or the labeling Claude) to recursively refine coarse patches that it finds too broad, rather than relying on the initial decomposer to hit the right granularity.

Motivation: even with PATCH-1 (feature-edge region growing) and PATCH-2 (concavity carve-out), the algorithm picks one global granularity. Some shapes want finer splits in certain regions and coarser elsewhere — e.g. a skull where the agent wants per-tooth patches on the mandible but a single patch for the parietal. A one-shot decomposer can't serve both cases; the agent or the labeling pass should be able to say 'subdivide this patch further' at its discretion.

Design sketch:
1. Extend the .tags.json format to carry a parent/child relationship: each patch has an optional 'parent' field and a 'children' array. Coarse patches stay in the tag set; refinement adds children without removing parents.
2. Add a 'subdivide_patch' primitive — takes a patch id, runs the SemanticPatchDecomposer algorithm restricted to that patch's vertex subset, and writes the resulting sub-patches as children.
3. Expose 'subdivide_patch' as both a CLI subcommand on PatchDecomposerCLI and a Daud tool so either the labeling Claude (during initial preprocessing) or the voyage agent (mid-replication) can invoke it.
4. mesh_compare_regions rolls errors up the parent chain so the agent can see 'left_mandible' chamfer even when its children 'left_molar_1..4' are the labeled leaves.

Non-goals: automatic granularity decisions. The agent decides when to subdivide.

Open questions: how to communicate the existence of subdivide_patch to the labeling Claude in the prompt without biasing it toward over-subdividing; how to handle patch-boundary edges that already mis-split a feature (a subdivision inherits the parent's boundary, so a bad parent boundary can't be fixed by children).

Originated from VOYAGE-51 Phase A discussion: user's comment 'if we can't get a perfect result from 1/2 it might be best to allow for recursive patch definitions at the behest of the agent doing the partition, but that is something for later'.
definition-of-done: Tag-sidecar format documented with parent/children fields. subdivide_patch exposed via CLI and Daud tool. mesh_compare_regions rolls up errors through the parent chain. Verified end-to-end on a reference where the labeling Claude (or the user manually) subdivides a coarse patch and the resulting tags.json round-trips through mesh_compare_regions cleanly.
testing-plan: Start from the skull tags.json produced by PATCH-1+PATCH-2. Manually call subdivide_patch on 'mandible' and confirm (a) children appear as 'mandible/tooth_*' or similar, (b) the parent is preserved, (c) mesh_compare_regions produces per-child chamfer plus a rolled-up parent number.
